events.description: Microsoft announces XNA at Game Developers Conference in San Jose, California, introducing the idea of a C#-friendly game development stack for Windows and Xbox.
XNA Game Studio Express opens the door for hobbyists, students, and independent developers to build games using C# and familiar .NET tooling.
Early open source efforts such as Mono.XNA begin exploring how the XNA model could work outside Microsoft’s own stack.
SilverSprite and XNA Touch push XNA-style development toward Silverlight, iPhone, and broader cross-platform use — important stepping stones toward MonoGame.
XNA Touch is used by several iPhone games, while XNA Game Studio 4.0 becomes Microsoft’s final major XNA release.
XNA Touch becomes MonoGame, moves to GitHub, and expands support across Android, macOS, Linux, and OpenGL on Windows.
MonoGame adds DirectX 11, Windows 8, and Windows Phone 8 support, launches its first website, and is presented at Microsoft’s //Build event.
Microsoft ends active XNA development. MonoGame 3.0 gives XNA developers a practical open source path forward.
MonoGame reaches PlayStation 4 and helps ship recognised games including TowerFall Ascension, Transistor, and Mercenary Kings.
The 3.4 release continues the project’s shift from XNA compatibility layer to stable, production-used framework.
The 3.5.1 release improves the framework and brings PlayStation Vita support to approved Sony developers.
The 3.6 release arrives, and Nintendo Switch support becomes available to approved Nintendo developers.
The 3.7 release continues the project’s long-running focus on portability, compatibility, and keeping existing games maintainable.
MonoGame 3.8 is released with major updates from the developer community and a clearer path for modern projects.
The 3.8.1 release lands, and PlayStation 5 support becomes available to approved Sony developers.
The MonoGame Foundation is formed to give the project a more sustainable structure for governance, funding, and long-term development.
The Foundation receives official 501(c)(3) non-profit status, retroactive to September 2023, and releases MonoGame 3.8.2.
The Foundation continues shipping more regularly, including MonoGame 3.8.4 and follow-up maintenance work for modern platform requirements.
Preview releases for 3.8.5 continue the modernisation work, including new project templates and additional graphics targets.
